sections.content: Austin, Texas has been one of the most talked-about real estate markets in the country for the past decade — and for good reason. Major employers like Tesla, Apple, Google, and Dell have planted roots here, drawing thousands of new residents every year. That demand creates real opportunity for investors who know how to find real estate deals in Austin TX before they hit the open market. Whether you're brand new to investing or looking to expand into a new city, this guide covers everything you need to know. If you're just getting started, check out our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide first — it'll give you a solid foundation before diving into a competitive market like Austin.
Austin TX Real Estate Market Overview

Austin's real estate market cooled significantly from its 2022 peak, when median home prices briefly touched $550,000. As of 2024, the median home price in Austin sits around $450,000 to $480,000 — still elevated compared to national averages, but more accessible than it was two years ago. Days on market have stretched from a few days to 30–60 days in many neighborhoods, giving investors more time and leverage to negotiate deals. Inventory is slowly rising, which is actually good news for deal hunters. More supply means more motivated sellers, more price reductions, and more opportunities to buy below market value.
The best time to buy real estate in a high-growth city isn't at the peak — it's during the correction, when everyone else has pulled back and deals are quietly sitting on the table.

Austin's long-term fundamentals remain strong. The city's population grew by over 33% between 2010 and 2020, and that growth hasn't stopped. The tech sector continues to expand, the University of Texas drives a steady renter base, and the city consistently ranks among the top metros for job growth and quality of life. For investors with a 5–10 year horizon, Austin remains a compelling market even at today's prices.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Austin
Not all Austin zip codes are created equal for investors. The right neighborhood depends on your strategy — wholesale, flip, or rental. Here's a breakdown of the areas worth your attention right now.
East Austin (78702, 78721)

East Austin has been the city's hottest transformation story over the past 10 years. Median prices here range from $400,000 to $650,000 depending on the block, but older homes on larger lots still trade below $400,000 — especially off-market. This area is ideal for fix-and-flip investors targeting buyers who want walkable neighborhoods, trendy restaurants, and proximity to downtown. ARVs (after-repair values) can push well past $600,000 on fully renovated properties, leaving solid margins for experienced flippers.
Southeast Austin (78744, 78747)

Southeast Austin is the value play right now. Median home prices range from $280,000 to $380,000, and rental demand is strong thanks to proximity to major employers and Austin-Bergstrom International Airport. Buy-and-hold investors can find homes in the $300,000 range that rent for $1,800 to $2,200 per month — not a home run cash flow play, but solid appreciation potential with reasonable entry points.
North Austin / Pflugerville (78660, 78664)

The suburbs north of Austin — particularly Pflugerville and Round Rock — offer some of the best opportunities for wholesalers and landlords in the metro. Home prices are lower (often $280,000–$350,000), there are more distressed and absentee-owner properties to target, and rental demand is steady from the large workforce population in the area. These markets fly under the radar compared to trendier Austin zip codes, which means less competition from other investors.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Austin TX
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is alive and well in Austin, but you need to work harder to find deals than you did in 2020 and 2021. The best wholesale opportunities come from distressed sellers — people facing foreclosure, divorce, probate, or inherited properties they don't want to manage. A typical wholesale deal in Austin might involve finding a property worth $420,000 ARV, negotiating a contract at $290,000, and assigning that contract to an end buyer for a $15,000–$25,000 assignment fee. To understand the full process, read our guide on [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners).
Fix-and-Flip Deals

Flippers in Austin are targeting the $350,000–$480,000 purchase range in neighborhoods like East Austin, South Austin (78704), and the Mueller district. A well-executed flip in these areas can yield $60,000–$120,000 in gross profit on a full renovation, though carrying costs, financing, and labor costs have all risen. Before you commit to a flip, use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to estimate your after-repair value and make sure your numbers actually work.
Rental Properties

Austin's rental market is strong, with average rents for a 3-bedroom home ranging from $1,900 to $2,800 depending on location. The University of Texas area creates demand for student housing, while the tech corridor drives demand from young professionals. Cash flow is tight at Austin's current price points, but appreciation and rent growth make long-term rentals attractive for investors not solely focused on immediate monthly returns.

Pro Tip: Before locking in any Austin deal, run the numbers through our free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator). Plug in your purchase price, estimated repairs, ARV, and desired profit margin to instantly see whether the deal works — before you make an offer.
How to Find Off-Market Deals in Austin

The best real estate deals in Austin TX never hit Zillow or the MLS. They're found through direct mail campaigns targeting absentee owners, driving for dollars in transitional neighborhoods, networking with local wholesalers and agents, and using data-driven tools to identify motivated sellers before anyone else does. Our in-depth guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) walks you through every strategy step by step. The short version: the investors winning in Austin right now are the ones building relationships and creating their own deal flow, not waiting for deals to come to them.

items: Target absentee owners in ZIP codes 78702, 78721, 78744, and 78660 with direct mail
Pull probate and pre-foreclosure lists from Travis County public records
Build relationships with local real estate attorneys who handle estate sales
Network with Austin REIA (Real Estate Investment Association) — they meet monthly
Use driving-for-dollars apps to identify vacant and distressed properties
Partner with a local agent who specializes in investor deals and off-market listings
Follow up — most motivated sellers need 5–7 contacts before they're ready to sell

sections.content: Austin Market Trends Investors Should Watch in 2024

Several trends are shaping the Austin investment landscape right now. First, new construction inventory is putting pressure on resale prices in the suburbs, which is good news for buyers but tough for flippers in those same areas. Second, short-term rental regulations in Austin have tightened — check current city ordinances before buying an Airbnb-intended property. Third, interest rates have kept many would-be buyers on the sidelines, which means rental demand stays elevated even as home prices soften. That's a useful dynamic for buy-and-hold investors. To dig deeper into deal analysis and financial modeling, read our guide on [How to Analyze Real Estate Deals Like a Pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) — it covers cap rates, cash-on-cash returns, and how to stress-test your numbers before you commit.
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Austin

Austin is a popular target for out-of-state investors, but remote investing requires a different approach than investing in your own backyard. Here's what you need to know before you start making offers from another state.

items: Build your team first: Find a local investor-friendly agent, property manager, contractor, and title company before you start making offers
Visit the market at least once: Austin neighborhoods vary dramatically block by block — photos and Google Street View don't tell the full story
Understand Texas-specific laws: Texas is a non-disclosure state, meaning sale prices aren't always publicly recorded — work with locals who have real comps
Focus on suburban markets initially: Pflugerville, Round Rock, and Kyle offer more forgiving price points and slower deal timelines — better for remote buyers learning the market
Use technology to your advantage: Platforms like AIWholesail help you identify and analyze Austin deals remotely using real-time data, so you can move fast when opportunity strikes
Factor in Texas property taxes: Property taxes in Travis County average 1.8–2.2% of assessed value — this significantly impacts your cash flow calculations compared to other states

sections.content: Out-of-state investing isn't about being everywhere at once. It's about building the right local team and using the right tools so the market works for you while you're not there.

Austin remains one of the most compelling real estate investment markets in the Sun Belt despite its price correction. The fundamentals — job growth, population growth, business-friendly environment — haven't changed. What has changed is that deals are actually available again. For investors willing to do the work, build relationships, and analyze deals carefully, 2024 could be an excellent entry point into the Austin market.
